Appearance:
MR YOGESHKUMAR A RATANPARA(7260) for the Applicant(s) No. 1 MR NAYAN D PAREKH(5010) for the Opponent(s) No. 1 ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE DEVAN M. DESAI  Date : 16/01/2024  ORAL ORDER 1. Heard learned advocate Mr.Yogeshkumar Ratanpara for the applicant.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. By invoking under Section 24 of the Civil Procedure Code, the applicant herein has prayed for transfer the proceedings of Family Suit No.1541 of 2023 from learned Family Court, Ahmedabad to the learned Principal Judge, Family Court, Junagadh.
3. Learned advocate for the applicant submits that the the marriage was solemnized with the present respondent - original plaintiff on 31.01.2013.
After some time of the marriage, the dispute between the present applicant and respondent - husband had cropped up.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/MCA/1337/2023 ORDER DATED: 16/01/2024 undefined

Therefore, the present applicant filed Hindu Marriage Petition No.9 of 2014 before the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge, Kehod under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 which came to be allowed on Priyankaben W/O Pratik Panchotia D/O ... vs Pratik Yogeshbhai Panchotia on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55350593/

sentences.text:
It is further submitted that the present applicant preferred Criminal Misc.
Application No.73 of 2022 for maintenance from the respondent-husband before the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Keshod Dist.- Junagadh under Section 125 of the Criminal Procedure Code,
which is pending.

entities.text: Chief Judicial Magistrate, Keshod Dist.- Junagadh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3.2 Thereafter, the applicant filed Criminal Misc. Application No.114 of 2013 before the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Keshod under Section 12 of the Domestic Violence Act, 2005,
which came to be partly allowed and directed the respondent to pay maintenance of Rs.4,500/- and Rs.1,000/- for house rent.

entities.text: Chief Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Keshod
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3.3 It is also submitted that the applicant -wife had lodged one FIR against the parents of the respondent - husband under Section 498(A) of the Indian Penal Code and also filed another FIR against the respondent under Sections 406, 420 and 114 of the Indian Penal Code and the criminal cases have been decided in the year 2023.

3.4 Learned advocate for the applicant has submitted NEUTRAL CITATION C/MCA/1337/2023 ORDER DATED: 16/01/2024 undefined that the respondent - husband has filed Family Suit No.1541 of 2023 seeking divorce before the learned Family Court, Ahmedabad under Section 13(A) of the Hindu Marriage Act.
3.5 It is further submitted that the applicant is residing at Keshod, Dist.Junagadh with her parents.
The distance between these cities i.e. from Junagadh to Ahmedabad is approximately 300 k.m. one way.
3.6 In view of the above submissions, learned advocate for the applicant urged to allow the present application.

4. The respondent-husband has filed Affidavit-in- reply and has mainly contended that he has paid an amount of Rs.6,42,500/- per annum towards maintenance and house rent to the applicant - wife and he has been acquitted by the Competent Court.
The respondent has taken contention that the father of the applicant - wife is a businessman and has showroom of ceramic tiles.
Hence, there is no issue of income.
Therefore, he has prayed to reject the present application.

5. It will not be out of place to refer the case of Sumita Singh Vs. Kumar Sanjay, AIR 2002 SC 396 ,
wherein NEUTRAL CITATION C/MCA/1337/2023 ORDER DATED: 16/01/2024 undefined the Apex Court has observed that the wife's inconvenience must be given due importance while deciding application under Section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

entities.text: Sumita Singh Vs. Kumar Sanjay, AIR 2002 SC 396
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The power under Section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is a discretionary power and Court may or may not exercise such discretion.

In the present case on hand, looking to the distance between Junagadh to Ahmedabad, it will be difficult for the applicant - wife to travel from Junagadh to Ahmedabad to attend the Court proceedings on each and every adjournment.

6. Having considered the averments made in the application and submissions advanced by the learned advocate for the applicant, it is clear that the petition filed by the opponent - husband before the Family Court, Ahmedabad, is far from Junagadh.
The applicant is residing at Junagadh with her parents, it would be very difficult for the applicant being a lady to attend the Court proceedings before the Family Court, Ahmedabad.

Priyankaben W/O Pratik Panchotia D/O ... vs Pratik Yogeshbhai Panchotia on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55350593/
2 7.

entities.text: Pratik Panchotia D/O ... vs Pratik Yogeshbhai Panchotia
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Under these circumstances, prayer made by the present applicant requires consideration and the same is allowed.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/MCA/1337/2023 ORDER DATED: 16/01/2024 undefined 7.1

Hence, the proceedings of Family Suit No.1541 of 2023 pending before the learned Family Court, Ahmedabad shall be transferred to the learned Principal Judge, Family Court, Junagadh for hearing and final disposal, in accordance with law.
8. With these observations and directions, the present application stands disposed of.
No order as to cost.
9. It is clarified that this Court has not expressed any opinion on the merits of the case.
Direct service is permitted.
